question: What is the primary point of entry for individuals into the national health system?
explanation: Primary Health Care serves as the first level of contact between the community and the health system. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is Primary Health Care positioned closest to where people live and work?

options.A: To reduce the financial burden of running large laboratories
options.B: To replace traditional healers in rural settlements
options.C: To provide advanced surgical operations at the village level
options.D: To ensure universal accessibility for everyday health needs

explanation: Placing care close to the population ensures that promotion, prevention, and basic treatment are easily reached by all households. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: In which year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care held?
explanation: The international conference that established modern Primary Health Care concepts took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: What major global goal was established by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Construction of teaching hospitals in every district
options.B: Free university education for all health workers
options.C: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.D: Total eradication of malaria across Africa

explanation: The conference set the ambitious global target of achieving health for the entire world population by the year 2000. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which principle ensures that health services are distributed fairly based on need?
explanation: Equity dictates that health care resources and services must reach vulnerable groups according to their actual health needs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is intersectoral collaboration necessary in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Nurses cannot manage community clinics without the presence of police officers
options.B: Ministries of health lack the financial capacity to buy any medications
options.C: Health outcomes are influenced by factors like education, agriculture, and housing
options.D: Hospitals must coordinate directly with manufacturing companies for supplies

explanation: Because broad social determinants shape community well-being, health sectors must cooperate with non-health sectors. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which service is considered an essential component of Primary Health Care?
explanation: Immunization is one of the foundational service components required at the primary care level. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: A community health clinic focuses on safe water supply and nutrition education. Which primary health care component does this reflect?

options.A: Basic environmental sanitation and food promotion

explanation: Safe water, sanitation, and nutritional support are core essential elements of grassroots primary health care delivery. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which tier of government in Nigeria bears primary responsibility for managing Primary Health Care?
explanation: Primary Health Care management in Nigeria is statutorily decentralized to the local government level. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is a major operational weakness commonly found in Nigerian primary health centers?

options.A: Overstaffing of medical consultants in rural dispensaries
options.B: Excessive availability of high-tech diagnostic equipment
options.C: Too many funds allocated for routine immunization programs
options.D: Frequent stockouts of essential drugs and poor infrastructure

explanation: Many primary facilities across the country suffer from infrastructural decay and shortages of basic medications and personnel. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why are strong referral linkages between primary and secondary health facilities important?

options.A: To ensure patients with complex conditions receive higher-level care promptly
options.B: To prevent community health workers from treating minor childhood fevers
options.C: To reduce the patient population at village clinics to zero
options.D: To ensure all medical funding goes directly to teaching hospitals

explanation: Effective referral systems guarantee that patients needing specialized interventions are transferred smoothly without unnecessary delays. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which strategy helps build trust and local ownership in community health programs?

options.B: Centralizing all clinics in the state capital

explanation: Involving respected local and religious figures encourages community participation and acceptance of health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)
